title: Given a Scenario, Troubleshoot Security Issues

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud security troubleshooting starts with identifying what security mechanism failed.

Access denied can indicate authentication or authorization. Failed secure communication can indicate an outdated cipher suite. Strange workload behavior can indicate exploitation or unauthorized software.
The mental model is: Who are you? → Authentication. What can you do? → Authorization. Is the software trusted, patched, and securely communicating? → Security configuration.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Is the issue proving identity, enforcing permissions, protecting credentials, using secure protocols, or preventing vulnerable or unauthorized software?
sections.callout: Cannot prove identity → authentication. Wrong permission → authorization. Unexpected elevated permission → privilege escalation. Stolen secret → leaked credentials.

sections.title: Cipher Suite Deprecations
paragraphs: A cipher suite defines cryptographic algorithms used to protect secure communication. Older suites may become unsafe and eventually be deprecated.
If one system still requires an obsolete cipher while another no longer allows it, secure communication may fail.
Think: The systems want encryption, but they no longer agree on a safe method.
sections.callout: Encrypted communication stops after an old cryptographic option is removed → cipher suite deprecation.

sections.title: Authorization Issues
paragraphs: Authorization determines what an authenticated identity is allowed to do.
A user can authenticate successfully and still encounter an authorization problem.
Think: We know who you are. The question is whether you are allowed to do this.
sections.callout: Login succeeds but the user cannot perform an action → authorization issue.

sections.title: Privilege Escalation
paragraphs: Privilege escalation occurs when an identity gains more permissions than it should have.
An attacker may exploit a vulnerability or configuration error to move from limited permissions to powerful privileges.
Think: A normal user becomes an administrator when they should not.
sections.callout: An account obtains higher privileges than intended → privilege escalation.

sections.title: Unauthorized Access
paragraphs: Unauthorized access occurs when a person, system, or process gains access to resources it should not be allowed to reach.
Think: They got in where they did not belong.
sections.callout: Someone accesses protected data or resources without proper permission → unauthorized access.

sections.title: Authentication Issues
paragraphs: Authentication determines whether an identity can prove who it claims to be.
Symptoms include login failures, invalid tokens, rejected credentials, and authentication service problems.
Think: Can you prove who you are?
sections.callout: The identity cannot successfully log in or prove itself → authentication issue.

sections.title: Leaked Credentials
paragraphs: Leaked credentials are passwords, API keys, tokens, or other authentication secrets exposed to unauthorized parties.
They may leak through source code, logs, misconfigured storage, phishing, or accidental disclosure.
Think: The key still works, but somebody who should not have it now has a copy.
sections.callout: A password, token, or API key has been exposed → leaked credentials.

sections.title: Software Vulnerability Issues
paragraphs: A software vulnerability is a weakness that can be exploited.
Security problems arise when software is outdated, unpatched, incorrectly configured, or uses vulnerable components.
Think: The attacker found a weakness in the software itself.
sections.callout: Exploitation is possible because of a known software flaw → software vulnerability issue.

sections.title: Unauthorized Software
paragraphs: Unauthorized software is installed or running without organizational approval.
It may introduce malware risk, unpatched vulnerabilities, unknown services, and compliance issues.
Think: If nobody approved it, nobody may be maintaining or securing it either.
sections.callout: Unknown or unapproved software appears on a cloud system → unauthorized software.

sections.title: Security Troubleshooting Flow
paragraphs: Can the identity log in? No → Authentication. Can the identity perform the required action? No → Authorization.
Does the identity have more rights than it should? Yes → Privilege escalation. Did somebody obtain credentials they should not have? Yes → Leaked credentials.
Did secure communication stop after cryptographic changes? Yes → Cipher suite deprecation. Is vulnerable or unapproved software involved? Yes → Software vulnerability or unauthorized software.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: An old encryption option is no longer accepted → Cipher suite deprecation
Login succeeds but an operation is denied → Authorization issue
A user becomes an administrator unexpectedly → Privilege escalation
A person accesses a resource without permission → Unauthorized access
A user cannot prove identity → Authentication issue
A password, API key, or token is exposed → Leaked credentials
A known exploitable flaw exists → Software vulnerability issue
An unapproved application is running → Unauthorized software

entries.title: Authentication vs. Authorization
paragraphs: Authentication happens first. Cannot log in means authentication. Can log in but cannot perform an action means authorization.

entries.title: Privilege Escalation vs. Unauthorized Access
paragraphs: Privilege escalation means a user gains a higher privilege level. Unauthorized access means a user gains access to something forbidden.
An attacker becoming an administrator is privilege escalation. Reading a confidential file without permission is unauthorized access.

entries.title: Leaked Credentials vs. Authentication Failure
paragraphs: Leaked credentials may authenticate successfully, which is what makes them dangerous. A stolen key can still work even though the person using it is not legitimate.

entries.title: Cipher Deprecation vs. General Network Failure
paragraphs: If basic connectivity exists but the encrypted session fails because an old cryptographic configuration is no longer accepted, choose cipher suite deprecation.

entries.title: Vulnerability vs. Unauthorized Software
paragraphs: Vulnerable software is approved or existing software that contains a weakness. Unauthorized software should not be present in the first place.
